headline: Sent $100,000 Bella Apartments Brightwood School redevelopment to committee; paused new food truck ordinance.
summary: The council approved eight grants and donations, including an $827,432.00 HOPWA grant on a 10-1-1 vote. It also passed resolutions supporting House Bill 4087 and the Springfield Central Cultural District. Council members discussed a proposed door-to-door sales ordinance and a youth commission change.
decisions: Approved the $15.00 FY27 Libraries cash donation, 12-0.
Approved the $3,847.00 Bass Pond Club aeration project donation, 12-0.
Approved the $100,000.00 FY27 TJO grant increase with no match required, 12-0.
Approved the $225,000.00 FY27 TJO grant with no match required, 12-0.
Approved the $490,523.00 FY27 SCSEP federal grant with an in-kind match, 12-0.
Approved the $765,803.05 FY27 Municipal Community Mitigation Fund grant with no match required, 12-0.
Approved the $827,432.00 FY27 HOPWA grant with no match required, 10-1 with one abstention.
Approved the $1,176,843.41 2026 WRAP funds grant with no match required, 12-0.
Approved $810.22 in bills of prior year for various departments, 12-0.
Approved the $116,466.08 Comcast franchise fee payment to the Cable PEG Access account, 12-0.
Approved the intergovernmental agreement with the Springfield Business Improvement District, 12-0.
Motion to table the food truck ordinance changes was withdrawn.
Approved a pause on the new food truck ordinance, 11-0 with Santaniello abstaining; the original ordinance stays in place.
Approved the resolution supporting House Bill 4087, 12-0.
Approved the resolution supporting the creation and sustaining of the Springfield Central Cultural District, 12-0.
Sent the $100,000.00 CPC item for the Bella Apartments redevelopment of Brightwood School to committee, 10-1 with one abstention.

 13. Amended Ordinance Chapter 279 Article VII — Door to Door Sales 
COUNCILOR MARTIN AND COUNCILOR HURST WORKED ON THIS ORDINANCE. 
 OTHER COMMUNITIES HAVE ADOPTED MORE STRICT GUIDELINES FOR DOOR TO 
DOOR SALES.  COUNCILOR MARTIN REFERENCED SOLAR PANEL SALES.  CAN 
ONLY WORK FROM 9A-6P AND MUST HAVE A LICENSE VISIBLE. 
COUNCILOR HURST REFERENCED A PERSONAL EXPERIENCE AT HIS OWN HOME. 
 REFERENCED WEST SPRINGFIELD UPDATED ORDINANCE.  WANTS THIS 
DISCUSSED IN THE NEIGHBORHOODS AS WELL AS GENERAL GOVERNMENT 
COMMITTEE. 
COUNCILOR EDWARDS WOULD LIKE TO FINE THE COMPANY FOR NON-
COMPLIANCE. 
COUNCILOR SANTANIELLO QUESTIONED THE FINE OF $300.  COUNCILOR HURST 
PROVIDED CLARIFICATION. 
COUNCILOR WALSH ASKED IF THIS WENT THROUGH THE LAW DEPARTMENT. 
 ALSO ENSURED IT IS FOR COMMERCIAL VENDORS. 
COUNCILOR FENTON WOULD LIKE TO SEE A RED LINED FROM THE ORIGINAL 
ORDINANCE.  ALSO WOULD LIKE TO SEE WHAT TYPE OF BACKGROUNDS WOULD 
BE GOING DOOR TO DOOR.  THESE ISSUES CAN BE DISCUSSED IN COMMITTEE. 
COUNCILOR DAVILA WANTED FOLKS AT HOME THAT IF YOU ARE 
UNCOMFORTABLE, THEN DO NOT OPEN THE DOOR.  IS IT POSSIBLE TO RESTRICT 
SUNDAYS?  ALSO, DO COMPANIES NEED TO NOTIFY THE POLICE DEPARTMENT? 
PRESIDENT WHITFIELD THANKED BOTH COUNCILORS.  GETS SALES PEOPLE ON A 
REGULAR BASIS.  WOULD LIKE TO SEE DAYS OFF AS WELL. 
 
AYES Brian Santaniello, Gerry Martin, Maria Perez, Zaida Govan, Kateri 
Walsh, Justin Hurst, Victor Davila, Michael Fenton, Jose Delgado, 
Lavar Click-Bruce, Melvin Edwards, Tracye Whitfield 
NAYS None 
AWAY None 
RECUSE None 
ABSTAIN None 
ABSENT Malo Brown 
 14. Amended Ordinance Chapter 279 Article VIII - Food Truck 
COUNCILOR CLICK-BRUCE ASKED TO TABLE THIS ITEM FOR THE REMAINDER OF 
THE SEASON.  PRESIDENT WHITFIELD ASKED FOR CLARIFICATION ON THE 120 
DAY PAUSE.  THE ORDINANCE WOULD GO INTO ACTION BY NOVEMBER SO THE 
COMMITTEE NEEDS TO TAKE ACTION.  COUNCILOR PEREZ NEEDED 
CLARIFICATION ON WHAT ITEMS WOULD BE DISCUSSED IN COMMITTEE. 
 COUNCILOR DAVILA INQUIRED IF 2 VOTES ARE NEEDED TO PAUSE.  COUNCILOR 
CLICK BRUCE WILL HOLD A MEETING THIS MONTH.  COUNCILOR GOVAN 
SUPPORTS TABLING.  PRESIDENT WHITFIELD CLARIFIED THAT THE NEW 
ORDINANCE WOULD BE PAUSED.  WOULD LIKE CLARITY BY THE NEXT COUNCIL 
MEETING IF THERE SHOULD BE 2 VOTES.  COUNCILOR HURST STATED A 2ND & 
FINAL ON THIS VOTE TO FINALIZE THE PAUSE.  COUNCILOR CLICK BRUCE 
WITHDREW HIS MOTION TO TABLE.  COUNCILOR CLICK BRUCE STATED THAT 
THE ORIGINAL ORDINANCE WOULD REMAIN IN PLACE. 
 
AYES Gerry Martin, Maria Perez, Zaida Govan, Kateri Walsh, Justin Hurst, 
Victor Davila, Michael Fenton, Jose Delgado, Lavar Click-Bruce, 
Melvin Edwards, Tracye Whitfield
NAYS None 
AWAY None

 15. Supporting House Bill 4087 
COUNCILOR CLICK BRUCE PRESENTED THE RESOLUTION STARTED BY 
REPRESENTATIVE ORLANDO RAMOS ON THE STATE LEVEL.  WANTS THIS 
ADOPTED IN THE CITY.  REFERENCED BOSTON ROAD BEING A RACE TRACK.  HE 
READ THE RESOLUTION INTO THE RECORD. 
COUNCILOR PEREZ STATED THAT BIRNIE AVE IS A DANGEROUS FREEWAY IN 
HER DISTRICT.  COUNCILOR HURST INQUIRED IF THE ACLU OR NAACP WAS 
CONTACTED ABOUT THE CIVIL RIGHTS ASPECT OF THE CAMERAS IN THIS 
RESOLUTION?  COUNCILOR CLICK BRUCE STATED THAT THIS RESOLUTION IS 
NOT TARGETING ANYONE AND MORE THAN WILLING TO HOLD MEETINGS WITH 
RESIDENTS.  COUNCILOR MARTIN ALSO WILLING TO HOLD PUBLIC SAFETY 
MEETINGS.  COUNCILOR GOVAN AGREES WITH COUNCILOR HURST TO PROCEED 
WITH CAUTION.  WOULD LIKE MORE DISCUSSION.  REFERENCED BERKSHIRE AVE 
IN HER DISTRICT.

 17. Amended Ordinance Chapter 16 Article V - Youth Commission (06/01/2026) 
COUNCILOR HURST ASKED TO HEAR THIS ITEM IN ADVANCE OF ITEM # 15. 
 COUNCILOR HURST TAKING THIS ITEM OUT OF UNFINISHED BUSINESS BASED 
ON COMMITTEE FEEDBACK.  PROPOSED THAT THE COUNCIL PRESIDENT OR 
DESIGNEE CAN APPOINT 3 OF THE 11 MEMBERS OF THE YOUTH COMMISSION. 
 COMMISSIONER CAULTON HARRIS STATED THAT SHENELL FORD WOULD BE 
TAKING THE LEAD AND OVERSEEING THE YOUTH COMMISSION. PRESIDENT 
WHITFIELD CLARIFIED THAT THE DIRECTOR OF PARKS WOULD BE REMOVED 
FROM THE BOARD.  COUNCILOR GOVAN STATED THAT INDIAN ORCHARD HAS A 
YOUTH COUNCIL. 
 
AYES Gerry Martin, Maria Perez, Zaida Govan, Kateri Walsh, Justin Hurst,

 18. Resolution Requesting Road and Sidewalk Repairs in East Forest Park (06/01/2026) 
 19. CPC - Bella Apartments Redevelopment Of Brightwood School - $100,000.00 (09/08/2026) 
COUNCILOR DAVILA WANTED TAKE THIS ITEM OUT OF UNFINISHED BUSINESS 
THERE WAS A MEETING HELD ON JUNE 22ND.  COUNCILOR HURST STATED THAT 
THERE SHOULD BE AN ASST CLERK PRESENT.  ATTORNEY SHEA STATED THERE
IS NO CONFLICT WITH THE CLERK FROM A LEGAL STANDPOINT.  COUNCILOR 
GOVAN OBJECTS TAKING THIS OUT OF UNFINISHED BUSINESS.  COUNCILOR 
HURST STATED THAT THE COUNCIL CANNOT VOTE ON THIS MATTER. 
COUNCILOR WALSH STATED THAT SHE IS UNCOMFORTABLE AND THERE 
SHOULD HAVE BEEN NOTICE.  COUNCILOR FENTON THAT THIS HAS BEEN UNDER 
UNFINISHED BUSINESS FOR MONTHS.  HE STATED THE LAW DEPARTMENT HAS 
ISSUED MEMOS.  EARLIER THIS EVENING THE COUNCIL VOTED ON A GRANT FOR 
NNCC.  THERE IS A RESPONSIBILITY TO TAKE ACTION ON THE ITEMS BEFORE 
THE BODY.  PRESIDENT WHITFIELD STATED THAT SHE WOULD NOT BE VOTING 
ON THIS TONIGHT.  WOULD LIKE THIS TO GO TO COMMITTEE.  COUNCILOR 
DAVILA WOULD LIKE TO TAKE ACTION BECAUSE IT WILL DIE ON OCTOBER 1ST. 
 REMINDED THAT THIS IS MONEY FOR SENIOR HOUSING.  CALLED RULE 18 TO 
BRING IT UP FOR VOTE.  COUNCILOR MARTIN SEES BOTH SIDES AND SAYS THE 
RESIDENTS DESERVE BETTER.  COUNCILOR GOVAN  WOULD LIKE A COMMITTEE 
MEETING.  COUNCILOR DAVILA READ RULE 18 INTO THE RECORD.  COUNCILOR 
PEREZ WAS NIGHT EXPECTING THIS TONIGHT.  WOULD LIKE TO SEE THE 
MATTER CONTINUED.  COUNCILOR WALSH WOULD LIKE THIS TO GO TO THE 
FINANCE COMMITTEE.  PRESIDENT CLARIFIED RULE 18, IT ONLY BRINGS THE 
ITEM TO COMMITTEE.  ATTY SHEA SPOKE ON THE MOTION TO SEND TO 
COMMITTEE.  THE CLOCK RESTARTS TODAY AT THIS MEETING. 
 
AYES Gerry Martin, Maria Perez, Zaida Govan, Kateri Walsh, Justin Hurst, 
Victor Davila, Jose Delgado, Lavar Click-Bruce, Melvin Edwards, 
Tracye Whitfield 
NAYS Michael Fenton 
AWAY None 
RECUSE None 
ABSTAIN Brian Santaniello 
ABSENT Malo Brown
